title: Does an input time offset really move the audio?
fullTitle: FFmpeg itsoffset Moves Audio 1.000 s: MP4 Keeps It in an Edit List

scenes.narration: You add input time offset one to the audio and copy the streams, no re-encode. Does the audio really move, in M P four and in M K V? We build a four second synthetic clip, run five cases, and read the start three ways.
captions: Does itsoffset with -c copy really move the audio?
Five cases, two containers, three readers.

scenes.chapter: A tone that marks the time
scenes.narration: The picture is one hundred different frames. The sound is silent until one and a half seconds, then a tone: our marker. As a control, a real delay filter moves the tone to two and a half seconds, while the container stamps stay at zero.
captions: Control: adelay moves the tone to 2.500 s, stamps stay at 0.

scenes.narration: Input time offset one on the audio, stream copy. In both containers the audio starts at exactly one second and the tone lands at two and a half. All one hundred ninety two thousand samples are unchanged. The picture stays at zero.
captions: Both files: audio start 1.000 s, tone 2.500 s, picture 0.000 s.
192000 samples equal the source. Three readers agree.

scenes.narration: In the M P four the second is an empty edit of one thousand milliseconds. Tell ffmpeg to ignore edit lists and the audio starts at zero again. In the M K V it is the time of the first audio block.
captions: mp4: empty edit of 1000 ms. -ignore_editlist 1: audio start 0.000 s.
mkv: first audio block at 1.000 s, picture block at 0.000 s.

scenes.narration: Now minus one. Both files end one second early, but built differently. The M P four keeps the picture at zero and skips the first forty eight thousand samples. The M K V keeps every sample and starts the picture at one second.
captions: mp4: 144000 samples decode, tone at 0.500 s, picture 0.000 s.
mkv: 192000 samples, tone at 1.500 s, picture starts 1.000 s.

scenes.narration: Put the offset on the video input instead and the shift is the same, the other way: the picture starts at one second, the audio at zero. In all ten files the hundred frames are the source frames, and copy changed no sample.
captions: itsoffset 1 on the video: audio -1.000 s against the picture.
10 files: 100 frames equal the source, audio equals the source.

scenes.narration: So input time offset really moves the audio, in both containers, and costs no quality. But in M P four it lives in an edit list that some readers skip. Check start times. Not tested: other builds, players, uploads, other codecs.
captions: It moves. Check start times, and whether your reader honors edit lists.
Not tested: other builds, players, uploads, AAC, subtitles.
